news.title: Déjà vu in Miami as FedEx MD-11 freighter overshoots runway
news.summary: A FedEx MD-11 cargo jet ran off the end of a Miami International runway in heavy rain, prompting a brief FAA ground stop but no injuries.
news.why: Miami is a key gateway for Latin American air cargo, so shippers with time-critical freight there should allow for short holiday-week delays and ask about MD-11 fleet availability.

news.title: 5 non-domiciled drivers want CDLs reinstated as battle separately moves through courts
news.summary: Five truck drivers who lost commercial licenses under the federal non-domiciled driver rule have petitioned for reinstatement while a court challenge to the rule is still pending.
news.why: The rule has pulled drivers out of the market, so the court outcome could loosen or tighten truckload capacity and spot rates heading into 2027 contract season.

news.title: US readies tariffs over manufacturing capacity, production concerns
news.summary: Washington is preparing tariffs of roughly 15% to 35% on goods from China, the EU and a dozen other partners after a Section 301 investigation into excess manufacturing capacity.
news.why: Importers should model landed costs at the top of that range now and review country-of-origin options before the rates are finalized.

news.title: Molson Coors, Primo Brands use fuel hedging to tackle logistics costs
news.summary: Two beverage makers explain how they lock in fuel prices to steady transport budgets, while experts warn hedging can be expensive and complex to manage.
news.why: With diesel swinging sharply this year, mid-size shippers can ask carriers for fixed or capped fuel surcharges as a simpler alternative to a formal hedge program.

news.title: EU to Temporarily Cap Hybrid Vehicle Imports from China
news.summary: Starting December 1 the EU will apply 200-day quotas on hybrid car imports, limiting Chinese-built hybrids to about 191,000 units, roughly half of expected volume, during an investigation.
news.why: Distributors of Chinese vehicles and parts for Europe should expect allocation fights and price moves, and may see diverted volume push into other markets.

news.title: Most Large Fuel Tankers Now Ship 'Dirty' Crude, Upending Trading
news.summary: A record three-quarters of big product tankers have switched to hauling crude because it pays better, leaving fewer ships to move refined fuels.
news.why: Tight product-tanker supply keeps diesel and jet fuel freight costs high, which flows straight into carrier fuel surcharges for shippers.

news.title: Red Sea and Indian Ocean Nations Advance Plans for Combined Maritime Security Force
news.summary: Coastal states around the Red Sea and western Indian Ocean are moving toward a joint naval task force to fight piracy and protect merchant traffic.
news.why: A regional force could eventually help Suez routings return, but importers should keep Cape of Good Hope transit times in their planning until it is operating.

news.title: India's State Shipping Giant Seeks Up to 22 New Ships in Major Domestic Shipbuilding Push
news.summary: The state-owned Shipping Corporation of India plans to add up to 22 vessels in a multibillion-dollar expansion tied to building more ships at home.
news.why: More Indian-flagged tonnage over the next few years could add capacity and pricing options on India trade lanes for buyers sourcing from the subcontinent.

news.title: Tech funding will rise in 2027, but AI investors will demand measurable savings
news.summary: Logistics tech funding hit $8.4 billion by mid-August and is on pace to beat 2025, while deal counts for logistics-tech acquisitions jumped about 74% year over year.
news.why: Expect vendors to pitch hard on proven ROI next year, so buyers evaluating AI tools should insist on pilots with measurable cost or service targets.

news.title: Dual-fuel fleet set to meet 20% of liner energy demand by 2030
news.summary: The World Shipping Council projects that ships able to burn renewable fuels will cover over a fifth of container-line energy needs around 2030, and it wants binding global rules to close the cost gap.
news.why: Green-fuel surcharges are likely to become a standard line on ocean invoices, so importers should ask carriers how they will price low-emission capacity.

news.title: Report: data center construction drives logistics services demand
news.summary: Interact Analysis finds the data center building boom is lifting demand for warehousing and material-handling automation, especially spare-parts and staging sites.
news.why: Electrical and cooling equipment buyers may face longer lead times and pricier warehouse space near major data center clusters.

news.title: USPS sees rising threat of holiday scams
news.summary: The Postal Service is warning about fake postage, brushing, impostor and mail-theft schemes, citing a survey in which most US consumers reported a holiday fraud attempt.
news.why: Ecommerce sellers should warn customers about fake delivery texts and check that discounted postage sources are legitimate to avoid seized parcels.

news.title: Automating your loading docks just got easier
news.summary: New robots for truck and container unloading are reaching real deployments, with one 3PL reporting robots clearing four to five containers per shift versus two to three by hand.
news.why: Importers paying high drayage detention or dock labor costs can ask their 3PLs whether automated unloading is on the roadmap and how it affects handling rates.
